sanskrit: tato rāmo mahātejā dhanur ādāya vīryavān kirīṭinaṃ mahākāyaṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ dadarśa ha
english: Then mighty Rāma, full of valour, took up his bow and beheld Kumbhakarṇa, the crown-wearing, immense-bodied one.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṃ parvatākāradarśanam kramamāṇam ivākāśaṃ purā nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum
english: Seeing that foremost of rākṣasas, who in appearance resembled a mountain, striding as if across the sky — like lord Nārāyaṇa of old —

sanskrit: satoyāmbudasaṃkāśaṃ kāñcanāṅgadabhūṣaṇam dṛṣṭvā punaḥ pradudrāva vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ
english: — like a rain-laden cloud, adorned with golden armlets — the great army of monkeys, beholding him, fled again in all directions.

sanskrit: vidrutāṃ vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā vardhamānaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ savismayam idaṃ rāmo vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha
english: Seeing the army in flight and the rākṣasa looming ever larger, Rāma spoke in wonder to Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: ko 'sau parvatasaṃkaśaḥ kirīṭī harilocanaḥ laṅkāyāṃ dṛśyate vīraḥ savidyud iva toyadaḥ
english: "Who is that hero visible in Laṅkā, resembling a mountain, wearing a crown, with tawny eyes, like a storm-cloud charged with lightning?"

sanskrit: pṛthivyāḥ ketubhūto 'sau mahān eko 'tra dṛśyate yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti tatas tataḥ
english: "That great one, sole banner of the earth, is seen here — at whose very sight all the monkeys scatter hither and thither."

sanskrit: ācakṣva me mahān ko 'sau rakṣo vā yadi vāsuraḥ na mayaivaṃvidhaṃ bhūtaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ kadā cana
english: "Tell me — who is this great being, rākṣasa or asura? Never before have I seen a creature of this kind."

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭo rājaputreṇa rāmeṇākliṣṭakāriṇā vibhīṣaṇo mahāprājñaḥ kākutstham idam abravīt
english: Thus questioned by the royal prince Rāma, the tireless doer, the supremely wise Vibhīṣaṇa spoke to the descendant of Kākutstha.

sanskrit: yena vaivasvato yuddhe vāsavaś ca parājitaḥ saiṣa viśravasaḥ putraḥ kumbhakarṇaḥ pratāpavān
english: "He by whom Vaivasvata Yama and Vāsava Indra were defeated in battle — he is that son of Viśravas, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa."

sanskrit: etena devā yudhi dānavāś ca yakṣā bhujaṃgāḥ piśitāśanāś ca gandharvavidyādharakiṃnarāś ca sahasraśo rāghava saṃprabhagnāḥ
english: "By him, O Rāghava, gods, dānavas, yakṣas, serpents, flesh-eaters, gandharvas, vidyādharas, and kiṃnaras — by the thousands — have been utterly routed in battle."

sanskrit: śūlapāṇiṃ virūpākṣaṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam hantuṃ na śekus tridaśāḥ kālo 'yam iti mohitāḥ
english: "The thirty gods could not slay the great-armed Kumbhakarṇa, trident in hand, of misshapen eyes — deluded, they thought: 'This is but Time itself.'"

sanskrit: prakṛtyā hy eṣa tejasvī kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ anyeṣāṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ varadānakṛtaṃ balam
english: "For Kumbhakarṇa is by nature radiant and mighty beyond measure; the power of other rākṣasa lords comes only from boons granted."

sanskrit: etena jātamātreṇa kṣudhārtena mahātmanā bhakṣitāni sahasrāṇi sattvānāṃ subahūny api
english: "By this great soul, even as a newborn tormented by hunger, thousands upon thousands of living creatures were devoured."

sanskrit: teṣu saṃbhakṣyamāṇeṣu prajā bhayanipīḍitāḥ yānti sma śaraṇaṃ śakraṃ tam apy arthaṃ nyavedayan
english: "As creatures were being consumed, the people, oppressed by fear, took refuge with Śakra and laid their grievance before him too."

sanskrit: sa kumbhakarṇaṃ kupito mahendro jaghāna vajreṇa śitena vajrī sa śakravajrābhihato mahātmā cacāla kopāc ca bhṛśaṃ nanāda
english: "Enraged, great Indra the thunderbolt-wielder struck Kumbhakarṇa with the sharp vajra; struck by Śakra's thunderbolt, that great soul reeled and roared mightily in fury."

sanskrit: tasya nānadyamānasya kumbhakarṇasya dhīmataḥ śrutvā ninādaṃ vitrastā bhūyo bhūmir vitatrase
english: "Hearing the roar of the wise Kumbhakarṇa as he bellowed, the earth was terrified and trembled anew."

sanskrit: tataḥ kopān mahendrasya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ vikṛṣyairāvatād dantaṃ jaghānorasi vāsavam
english: "Then, in anger at great Indra, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa wrenched a tusk from Airāvata and struck Vāsava upon the chest."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaprahārārto vicacāla sa vāsavaḥ tato viṣeduḥ sahasā devabrahmarṣidānavāḥ
english: "Wounded by Kumbhakarṇa's blow, Vāsava staggered; thereupon gods, brahmarṣis, and dānavas all fell into sudden despair."

sanskrit: prajābhiḥ saha śakraś ca yayau sthānaṃ svayambhuvaḥ kumbhakarṇasya daurātmyaṃ śaśaṃsus te prajāpateḥ prajānāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ cāpi devānāṃ cāpi dharṣaṇam
english: "And Śakra, together with the people, went to the abode of the Self-born; they reported to Prajāpati Kumbhakarṇa's wickedness, his devouring of creatures, and his assaulting of the gods."

sanskrit: evaṃ prajā yadi tv eṣa bhakṣayiṣyati nityaśaḥ acireṇaiva kālena śūnyo loko bhaviṣyati
english: "If he continues to devour creatures thus without cease, in no long time the world will be empty."

sanskrit: vāsavasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ rakṣāṃsy āvāhayām āsa kumbhakarṇaṃ dadarśa ha
english: "Hearing Vāsava's words, the Grandfather of all worlds summoned the rākṣasas and beheld Kumbhakarṇa."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaṃ samīkṣyaiva vitatrāsa prajāpatiḥ dṛṣṭvā niśvasya caivedaṃ svayambhūr idam abravīt
english: "On beholding Kumbhakarṇa, Prajāpati was seized with fear; having looked and sighed, the Self-born spoke these words."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ lokavināśāya paurastyenāsi nirmitaḥ tasmāt tvam adya prabhṛti mṛtakalpaḥ śayiṣyasi brahmaśāpābhibhūto 'tha nipapātāgrataḥ prabhoḥ
english: "'Surely you were fashioned by the Progenitor for the destruction of worlds; therefore from this day forth you shall sleep as one dead.' Overcome by Brahmā's curse, he fell prostrate before the lord."

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃbhrānto rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt vivṛddhaḥ kāñcano vṛkṣaḥ phalakāle nikṛtyate
english: "Then greatly agitated, Rāvaṇa spoke: 'A golden tree grown to fullness is cut down at the very time of its fruit!'"

sanskrit: na naptāraṃ svakaṃ nyāyyaṃ śaptum evaṃ prajāpate na mithyāvacanaś ca tvaṃ svapsyaty eṣa na saṃśayaḥ kālas tu kriyatām asya śayane jāgare tathā
english: "'It is not right, O Prajāpati, to curse one's own grandson thus — and your word is never false; he shall sleep, there is no doubt; but let a term be set for his sleeping and his waking.'"

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā svayambhūr idam abravīt śayitā hy eṣa ṣaṇ māsān ekāhaṃ jāgariṣyati
english: "Hearing Rāvaṇa's words, the Self-born spoke: 'He shall sleep for six months at a stretch and wake for a single day.'"

sanskrit: ekenāhnā tv asau vīraś caran bhūmiṃ bubhukṣitaḥ vyāttāsyo bhakṣayel lokān saṃkruddha iva pāvakaḥ
english: "Within that one day that hero, roaming the earth in hunger, with gaping mouth shall devour the worlds, like fire blazing in fury."

sanskrit: so 'sau vyasanam āpannaḥ kumbhakarṇam abodhayat tvatparākramabhītaś ca rājā saṃprati rāvaṇaḥ
english: "That king Rāvaṇa, having fallen into calamity, and now afraid of your might, has wakened Kumbhakarṇa."

sanskrit: sa eṣa nirgato vīraḥ śibirād bhīmavikramaḥ vānarān bhṛśasaṃkruddho bhakṣayan paridhāvati
english: "He, the hero of terrifying valour, has now emerged from the camp and runs about devouring the monkeys in great fury."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇaṃ samīkṣyaiva harayo vipradudruvuḥ katham enaṃ raṇe kruddhaṃ vārayiṣyanti vānarāḥ
english: "Simply at the sight of Kumbhakarṇa, the monkeys have fled in terror — how shall the vānaras restrain him when he is enraged in battle?"

sanskrit: ucyantāṃ vānarāḥ sarve yantram etat samucchritam iti vijñāya harayo bhaviṣyantīha nirbhayāḥ
english: "Let all the monkeys be told: 'This is a machine set up' — knowing this, the monkeys will be fearless."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutvā hetumat sumukhodgatam uvāca rāghavo vākyaṃ nīlaṃ senāpatiṃ tadā
english: Hearing the reasoned words issuing clearly from Vibhīṣaṇa's mouth, Rāghava then spoke to Nīla the army commander.

sanskrit: gaccha sainyāni sarvāṇi vyūhya tiṣṭhasva pāvake dvārāṇy ādāya laṅkāyāś caryāś cāpy atha saṃkramān
english: "Go, array all the troops and stand firm in battle formation; seize the gates of Laṅkā, and likewise her highways and bridges."

sanskrit: śailaśṛṅgāṇi vṛkṣāṃś ca śilāś cāpy upasaṃharan tiṣṭhantu vānarāḥ sarve sāyudhāḥ śailapāṇayaḥ
english: "Gathering mountain peaks, trees, and boulders, let all the monkeys stand ready, armed, rocks in hand."

sanskrit: rāghaveṇa samādiṣṭo nīlo haricamūpatiḥ śaśāsa vānarānīkaṃ yathāvat kapikuñjaraḥ
english: Instructed by Rāghava, Nīla, commander of the monkey host, that elephant among monkeys, duly marshalled the vānara army.

sanskrit: tato gavākṣaḥ śarabho hanumān aṅgado nalaḥ śailaśṛṅgāṇi śailābhā gṛhītvā dvāram abhyayuḥ
english: Then Gavākṣa, Śarabha, Hanūmān, Aṅgada, and Nala — mountain-like in form — grasping mountain peaks, advanced upon the gate.

sanskrit: tato harīṇāṃ tad anīkam ugraṃ rarāja śailodyatavṛkṣahastam gireḥ samīpānugataṃ yathaiva mahan mahāmbhodharajālam ugram
english: Then that fierce array of monkeys, trees and upraised peaks in their hands, drawn up near the mountain, shone resplendent — like a vast, threatening mass of storm-clouds.

sanskrit: sa tu rākṣasaśārdūlo nidrāmadasamākulaḥ rājamārgaṃ śriyā juṣṭaṃ yayau vipulavikramaḥ
english: That tiger among rākṣasas, still stupefied with the intoxication of sleep, strode with vast steps along the royal road, adorned in splendour.

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ sahasraiś ca vṛtaḥ paramadurjayaḥ gṛhebhyaḥ puṣpavarṣeṇa kāryamāṇas tadā yayau
english: Surrounded by thousands of rākṣasas, utterly invincible, with a rain of flowers poured upon him from the houses, he went on his way.

sanskrit: sa hemajālavitataṃ bhānubhāsvaradarśanam dadarśa vipulaṃ ramyaṃ rākṣasendraniveśanam
english: He beheld the vast and beautiful dwelling of the rākṣasa lord, spread over with nets of gold, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: sa tat tadā sūrya ivābhrajālaṃ praviśya rakṣo'dhipater niveśanam dadarśa dūre 'grajam āsanasthaṃ svayambhuvaṃ śakra ivāsanastham
english: Entering that abode of the rākṣasa lord like the sun passing through a canopy of clouds, he saw his elder brother seated in the distance, like the Self-born enthroned, like Śakra upon his throne.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya gṛhaṃ bhrātuḥ kakṣyām abhivigāhya ca dadarśodvignam āsīnaṃ vimāne puṣpake gurum
english: Approaching his brother's house and penetrating to the inner court, he saw his overlord seated in anxious grief upon the Puṣpaka aerial palace.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇam upasthitam tūrṇam utthāya saṃhṛṣṭaḥ saṃnikarṣam upānayat
english: Then seeing Kumbhakarṇa arrived before him, the ten-necked one rose quickly, delighted, and drew him near.

sanskrit: athāsīnasya paryaṅke kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ bhrātur vavande caraṇāṃ kiṃ kṛtyam iti cābravīt utpatya cainaṃ mudito rāvaṇaḥ pariṣasvaje
english: Then mighty Kumbhakarṇa, as his brother sat upon the couch, bowed at his feet and asked: "What is to be done?" Springing up, Rāvaṇa joyfully embraced him.

sanskrit: sa bhrātrā saṃpariṣvakto yathāvac cābhinanditaḥ kumbhakarṇaḥ śubhaṃ divyaṃ pratipede varāsanam
english: Embraced by his brother and duly honoured, Kumbhakarṇa took his seat upon a fair and splendid throne.

sanskrit: sa tadāsanam āśritya kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ saṃraktanayanaḥ kopād rāvaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Seated there, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, his eyes flushed red with anger, addressed Rāvaṇa with these words.

sanskrit: kimartham aham ādṛtya tvayā rājan prabodhitaḥ śaṃsa kasmād bhayaṃ te 'sti ko 'dya preto bhaviṣyati
english: "For what purpose have I, O king, been respectfully roused by you? Tell me — from what do you fear? Who is to become a ghost today?"

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ rāvaṇaḥ kruddhaṃ kumbhakarṇam avasthitam īṣat tu parivṛttābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Rāvaṇa spoke to his brother Kumbhakarṇa, who sat there in anger, with eyes slightly averted.

sanskrit: adya te sumahān kālaḥ śayānasya mahābala sukhitas tvaṃ na jānīṣe mama rāmakṛtaṃ bhayam
english: "A very great time has passed while you slept, O mighty one; complacent, you have not known the fear that Rāma has brought upon me."

sanskrit: eṣa dāśarathī rāmaḥ sugrīvasahito balī samudraṃ sabalas tīrtvā mūlaṃ naḥ parikṛntati
english: "This Rāma, son of Daśaratha, mighty with Sugrīva at his side, has crossed the ocean with his army and is cutting at our very root."

sanskrit: hanta paśyasva laṅkāyā vanāny upavanāni ca setunā sukham āgamya vānaraikārṇavaṃ kṛtam
english: "Look — see how the groves and gardens of Laṅkā are now an ocean of monkeys, arrived with ease across the bridge."

sanskrit: ye rākṣasā mukhyatamā hatās te vānarair yudhi vānarāṇāṃ kṣayaṃ yuddhe na paśyāmi kadā cana
english: "The foremost of the rākṣasas have been slain by the monkeys in battle; a diminishing of the monkeys in combat I see never at all."

sanskrit: sarvakṣapitakośaṃ ca sa tvam abhyavapadya mām trāyasvemāṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ bālavṛddhāvaśeṣitām
english: "With the treasury entirely exhausted, you have come to me — protect this city of Laṅkā, left with only the young and the old."

sanskrit: bhrātur arthe mahābāho kuru karma suduṣkaram mayaivaṃ noktapūrvo hi kaś cid bhrātaḥ paraṃtapa tvayy asti mama ca snehaḥ parā saṃbhāvanā ca me
english: "For your brother's sake, O mighty-armed one, perform this most difficult deed — I have never before spoken thus to anyone, O brother, scorcher of foes; in you I place my love and my highest hope."

sanskrit: devāsuravimardeṣu bahuśo rākṣasarṣabha tvayā devāḥ prativyūhya nirjitāś cāsurā yudhi na hi te sarvabhūteṣu dṛśyate sadṛśo balī
english: "In the many fierce battles between gods and asuras, O bull among rākṣasas, you have stood against the gods and conquered asuras in battle — among all beings no equal to your might is seen."

sanskrit: kuruṣva me priyahitam etad uttamaṃ yathāpriyaṃ priyaraṇabāndhavapriya svatejasā vidhama sapatnavāhinīṃ śaradghanaṃ pavana ivodyato mahān
english: "Do for me this highest deed of love and benefit, O dear one who loves dear battle-comrades — scatter the enemy host by your own brilliance, like a great wind rising to dispel the autumn clouds."

sanskrit: tasya rākṣasarājasya niśamya paridevitam kumbhakarṇo babhāṣe 'tha vacanaṃ prajahāsa ca
english: Hearing the lamentation of the rākṣasa king, Kumbhakarṇa then spoke, and laughed.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭo doṣo hi yo 'smābhiḥ purā mantravinirṇaye hiteṣv anabhiyuktena so 'yam āsāditas tvayā
english: "The fault we foresaw long ago in the counsel chamber — you who were not intent on what is beneficial have now encountered that very consequence."

sanskrit: śīghraṃ khalv abhyupetaṃ tvāṃ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ nirayeṣv eva patanaṃ yathā duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ
english: "Indeed the fruit of evil action has swiftly come upon you — like the fall into hell of one who has done wicked deeds."

sanskrit: prathamaṃ vai mahārāja kṛtyam etad acintitam kevalaṃ vīryadarpeṇa nānubandho vicāritaḥ
english: "In the first place, O great king, this deed was undertaken without thought; relying solely on pride in your prowess, you gave no consideration to its consequences."

sanskrit: yaḥ paścāt pūrvakāryāṇi kuryād aiśvaryam āsthitaḥ pūrvaṃ cottarakāryāṇi na sa veda nayānayau
english: "He who, placed in sovereignty, does first what should be done later and does later what should be done first — such a one knows nothing of sound policy and its contrary."

sanskrit: deśakālavihīnāni karmāṇi viparītavat kriyamāṇāni duṣyanti havīṃṣy aprayateṣv iva
english: "Actions performed in the wrong place and time, done in a contrary manner, come to ruin — like oblations offered by one who has not purified himself."

sanskrit: trayāṇāṃ pañcadhā yogaṃ karmaṇāṃ yaḥ prapaśyati sacivaiḥ samayaṃ kṛtvā sa sabhye vartate pathi
english: "He who clearly sees the fivefold application of the three types of action and, having taken counsel with his ministers, follows the right course — such a one walks the proper path of governance."

sanskrit: yathāgamaṃ ca yo rājā samayaṃ vicikīrṣati budhyate sacivān buddhyā suhṛdaś cānupaśyati
english: "A king who seeks to devise policy in accordance with scripture, who understands his ministers with discernment, and who keeps watch over his allies —"

sanskrit: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca sarvān vā rakṣasāṃ pate bhajate puruṣaḥ kāle trīṇi dvandvāni vā punaḥ
english: "— that man, O lord of rākṣasas, pursues all three — dharma, artha, and kāma — in their season, or again in their three paired combinations."

sanskrit: triṣu caiteṣu yac chreṣṭhaṃ śrutvā tan nāvabudhyate rājā vā rājamātro vā vyarthaṃ tasya bahuśrutam
english: "A king or one of royal standing who, after hearing what is foremost among these three, does not comprehend it — his wide learning is in vain."

sanskrit: upapradānaṃ sāntvaṃ vā bhedaṃ kāle ca vikramam yogaṃ ca rakṣasāṃ śreṣṭha tāv ubhau ca nayānayau
english: "Conciliation by gifts, conciliation by gentle speech, sowing dissension, and bold action at the right moment — these strategies, O foremost of rākṣasas, and both sound and unsound policy —"

sanskrit: kāle dharmārthakāmān yaḥ saṃmantrya sacivaiḥ saha niṣevetātmavāṃl loke na sa vyasanam āpnuyāt
english: "— he who, self-possessed, takes counsel with his ministers in due season regarding dharma, artha, and kāma, and then acts upon them, encounters no calamity in this world."

sanskrit: hitānubandham ālokya kāryākāryam ihātmanaḥ rājā sahārthatattvajñaiḥ sacivaiḥ saha jīvati
english: "A king lives well who, with ministers versed in the true meaning of policy, examines what is to be done and what is not, in view of the chain of consequences beneficial to himself."

sanskrit: anabhijñāya śāstrārthān puruṣāḥ paśubuddhayaḥ prāgalbhyād vaktum icchanti mantreṣv abhyantarīkṛtāḥ
english: "Men of animal understanding, ignorant of the import of the śāstras, yet presume to speak in councils to which they have been admitted — solely out of arrogance."

sanskrit: aśāstraviduṣāṃ teṣāṃ na kāryam ahitaṃ vacaḥ arthaśāstrānabhijñānāṃ vipulāṃ śriyam icchatām
english: "The words of those who do not know the śāstras, who are ignorant of the science of polity and yet covet great prosperity, should not be made welcome."

sanskrit: ahitaṃ ca hitākāraṃ dhārṣṭyāj jalpanti ye narāḥ avekṣya mantrabāhyās te kartavyāḥ kṛtyadūṣaṇāḥ
english: "Those who, through impudence, prattle that the harmful is beneficial must be watched and excluded from counsel as destroyers of enterprise."

sanskrit: vināśayanto bhartāraṃ sahitāḥ śatrubhir budhaiḥ viparītāni kṛtyāni kārayantīha mantriṇaḥ
english: "Ministers who, in league with clever enemies, cause the destruction of their master by setting contrary courses of action in motion here —"

sanskrit: tān bhartā mitrasaṃkāśān amitrān mantranirṇaye vyavahāreṇa jānīyāt sacivān upasaṃhitān
english: "— a master should recognise those ministers, who resemble friends but are enemies in counsel, through their conduct, even as they are brought close."

sanskrit: capalasyeha kṛtyāni sahasānupradhāvataḥ chidram anye prapadyante krauñcasya kham iva dvijāḥ
english: "The affairs of a fickle man who rushes headlong into things are exploited by others, as birds enter the gap in the Krauñca mountain."

sanskrit: yo hi śatrum avajñāya nātmānam abhirakṣati avāpnoti hi so 'narthān sthānāc ca vyavaropyate
english: "He who, while disregarding the enemy, does not protect himself, truly incurs disaster and is dislodged from his position."

sanskrit: tat tu śrutvā daśagrīvaḥ kumbhakarṇasya bhāṣitam bhrukuṭiṃ caiva saṃcakre kruddhaś cainam uvāca ha
english: Hearing Kumbhakarṇa's speech, the ten-necked one drew his brows together and, enraged, spoke to him thus.

sanskrit: mānyo gurur ivācāryaḥ kiṃ māṃ tvam anuśāsati kim evaṃ vākśramaṃ kṛtvā kāle yuktaṃ vidhīyatām
english: "Like a venerable teacher and preceptor — why do you lecture me? Why this laborious rhetoric? Let what is proper be done now, at this moment."

sanskrit: vibhramāc cittamohād vā balavīryāśrayeṇa vā nābhipannam idānīṃ yad vyarthās tasya punaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "Whether it was done through confusion, delusion of mind, or reliance on strength and valour — what is now done cannot be undone; do not pointlessly repeat it."

sanskrit: asmin kāle tu yad yuktaṃ tad idānīṃ vidhīyatām mamāpanayajaṃ doṣaṃ vikrameṇa samīkuru
english: "Let what is now fitting at this juncture be enacted; remedy by your valour the fault arising from my ill-counsel."

sanskrit: yadi khalv asti me sneho bhrātṛtvaṃ vāvagacchasi yadi vā kāryam etat te hṛdi kāryatamaṃ matam
english: "If indeed you have affection for me, if you recognise the bond of brotherhood, or if this matter is regarded by you at heart as most urgent —"

sanskrit: sa suhṛdyo vipannārthaṃ dīnam abhyavapadyate sa bandhur yo 'panīteṣu sāhāyyāyopakalpate
english: "— he is a friend who comes to the aid of one whose affairs have gone to ruin and who is brought low; he is a kinsman who lends his help when things have gone wrong."

sanskrit: tam athaivaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu vacanaṃ dhīradāruṇam ruṣṭo 'yam iti vijñāya śanaiḥ ślakṣṇam uvāca ha
english: Then perceiving that Rāvaṇa was offended by these words — firm yet harsh — Kumbhakarṇa spoke softly and soothingly.

sanskrit: atīva hi samālakṣya bhrātaraṃ kṣubhitendriyam kumbhakarṇaḥ śanair vākyaṃ babhāṣe parisāntvayan
english: Observing too keenly that his brother's senses were agitated, Kumbhakarṇa spoke gently, consoling him.

sanskrit: alaṃ rākṣasarājendra saṃtāpam upapadya te roṣaṃ ca saṃparityajya svastho bhavitum arhasi
english: "Enough — O lord of rākṣasa kings, do not give yourself over to anguish; casting aside your rage, you ought to be at peace."

sanskrit: naitan manasi kartavvyaṃ mayi jīvati pārthiva tam ahaṃ nāśayiṣyāmi yatkṛte paritapyase
english: "While I yet live, O king, this matter ought not to weigh upon your mind; I shall destroy him on whose account you grieve."

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu hitaṃ vācyaṃ sarvāvasthaṃ mayā tava bandhubhāvād abhihitaṃ bhrātṛsnehāc ca pārthiva
english: "Surely I must in every situation speak what is beneficial to you — what I said was spoken from the bond of kinship and from brotherly love, O king."

sanskrit: sadṛśaṃ yat tu kāle 'smin kartuṃ snigdhena bandhunā śatrūṇāṃ kadanaṃ paśya kriyamāṇaṃ mayā raṇe
english: "What now befits a devoted kinsman at this moment — behold it being done by me: the destruction of enemies in battle."

sanskrit: adya paśya mahābāho mayā samaramūrdhani hate rāme saha bhrātrā dravantīṃ harivāhinīm
english: "This very day, O mighty-armed one, behold — with Rāma and his brother slain by me at the front of battle — the monkey host in flight."

sanskrit: adya rāmasya tad dṛṣṭvā mayānītaṃ raṇāc chiraḥ sukhībhava mahābāho sītā bhavatu duḥkhitā
english: "Today, seeing Rāma's head brought from the battlefield by me, be glad, O mighty-armed one; let Sītā be made to grieve."

sanskrit: adya rāmasya paśyantu nidhanaṃ sumahat priyam laṅkāyāṃ rākṣasāḥ sarve ye te nihatabāndhavāḥ
english: "Today let all the rākṣasas in Laṅkā — those whose kinsmen have been slain — behold the greatly desired death of Rāma."

sanskrit: adya śokaparītānāṃ svabandhuvadhakāraṇāt śatror yudhi vināśena karomy asrapramārjanam
english: "Today, by the destruction of the enemy in battle, I shall wipe away the tears of those overcome with grief at the slaying of their own kinsmen."

sanskrit: adya parvatasaṃkāśaṃ sasūryam iva toyadam vikīrṇaṃ paśya samare sugrīvaṃ plavageśvaram
english: "Today behold Sugrīva, lord of the leaping monkeys, mountain-like, like a cloud bearing the sun, shattered in battle."

sanskrit: na paraḥ preṣaṇīyas te yuddhāyātula vikrama aham utsādayiṣyāmi śatrūṃs tava mahābala
english: "No other need be sent by you to battle, O one of incomparable prowess — I myself, O mighty one, shall annihilate your enemies."

sanskrit: yadi śakro yadi yamo yadi pāvakamārutau tān ahaṃ yodhayiṣyāmi kubera varuṇāv api
english: "Whether it be Śakra, or Yama, or fire and wind, or Kubera and Varuṇa — I shall fight all of them."

sanskrit: girimātraśarīrasya śitaśūladharasya me nardatas tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrasya bibhīyāc ca puraṃdaraḥ
english: "Even Puraṃdara Indra should fear me, whose body is the size of a mountain, who wields a sharp trident, who roars, whose fangs are keen."

sanskrit: atha vā tyaktaśastrasya mṛdgatas tarasā ripūn na me pratimukhe kaś cic chaktaḥ sthātuṃ jijīviṣuḥ
english: "Or else, abandoning weapons, treading down the enemies with swift force — no one who wishes to live is capable of standing before me in battle."

sanskrit: naiva śaktyā na gadayā nāsinā na śitaiḥ śaraiḥ hastābhyām eva saṃrabdho haniṣyāmy api vajriṇam
english: "Neither with spear, nor with mace, nor with sword, nor with keen arrows — but with my two bare hands, in fury, I shall slay even the thunderbolt-wielder."

sanskrit: yadi me muṣṭivegaṃ sa rāghavo 'dya sahiṣyati tataḥ pāsyanti bāṇaughā rudhiraṃ rāghavasya te
english: "If that Rāghava today withstands the force of my fist, then let the torrents of arrows drink Rāghava's blood."

sanskrit: cintayā bādhyase rājan kimarthaṃ mayi tiṣṭhati so 'haṃ śatruvināśāya tava niryātum udyataḥ
english: "Why are you tormented by anxiety, O king, when I am at hand? I am ready to go forth for the destruction of your enemy."

sanskrit: muñca rāmād bhayaṃ rājan haniṣyāmīha saṃyuge rāghavaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sugrīvaṃ ca mahābalam asādhāraṇam icchāmi tava dātuṃ mahad yaśaḥ
english: "Release your fear of Rāma, O king; in combat I shall slay Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa, and the mighty Sugrīva — I wish to bestow upon you extraordinary and great glory."

sanskrit: vadhena te dāśaratheḥ sukhāvahaṃ sukhaṃ samāhartum ahaṃ vrajāmi nihatya rāmaṃ sahalakṣmaṇena khādāmi sarvān hariyūthamukhyān
english: "To bring you pleasure-bringing joy through the slaying of the son of Daśaratha, I go forth; having slain Rāma along with Lakṣmaṇa, I shall devour all the chiefs of the monkey host."

sanskrit: ramasva kāmaṃ piba cāgryavāruṇīṃ kuruṣva kṛtyāni vinīyatāṃ jvaraḥ mayādya rāme gamite yamakṣayaṃ cirāya sītā vaśagā bhaviṣyati
english: "Revel at will, drink choice wine, attend to your affairs, let your fever be allayed; when I have this very day dispatched Rāma to Yama's realm, Sītā will at last be yours to command."
